# Client Diversity and Economies of Variety

Around a decade ago, when Lean Thinking was still popular, I wrote a post called [Fat Thinking and Economies of Variety](https://ribbonfarm.com/2016/07/28/fat-thinking-and-economies-of-variety/)

Later, I learned about the idea of client diversity as a measure of resilience from the Ethereum world. That’s one feature that distinguishes it from Bitcoin which believes in the One True Client. In practice client diversity is a tradeoff curve. The resilience only exists if enough people are using several clients, creating monoculture failure insurance. But this means keeping a flock of clients loosely in sync with an evolving protocol is harder and the necessary orchestration slows things down. The opposite of _move fast and break things_ is _move slowly and diversify things._ Ethereum has found an uneasy balance. Geth still dominates but there are other serious candidates. 

Farcaster and Bluesky offer counter-lessons. I don’t think either ever really achieved enough client diversity to be worth it. I’m not sure what lesson to take from this.

AI though, changes the game entirely. If almost anyone can vibecode a client against a spec, and (unlike Ethereum) there isn’t much need for tight consensus in the presence of serious exploit incentives (like MEV), you can start to approach the Old Nature standard of n=1 maximal “client” diversity against the “DNA” spec. 

I think Blygger hits the sweet spot. There’s low consensus need, low security concerns, and an enshrined decision to leave all presentation decisions that do not affect communication semantics to the clients. 

But there’s more. I think being backward compatible with RSS and WebMention while introducing novel primitives drives not just client diversity against known patterns (like Farcaster and Bluesky can reproduce many familiar patterns like “Twitter” or “Blog” or “Instagram”), but client _innovation._ the cost of this permissioning of innovation is you have to give up any sort of global feed. There’s only the local feed assembled from your blygger and RSS inputs. I think this is a necessary condition for approaching biological levels of client diversity. An active innovation frontier is not optional. This of course creates enormous centrifugal divergence pressure, which makes some nice things much harder.

BUT the protocol is so minimal, (RISCy?) I think you could do the equivalent of Ethereum L2s with extra standards or protocols. Blygger extensions basically. RISC-V has this philosophy too. There are various extensions. You can imagine a Blygger Extension standard that lets people interested in photography share an Instagram-style presentation spec, with any needed protocol-level specs either tunneling through (like identity does on _author_), or being proposed as MAY semantics that uninterested clients can just ignore.

This ventures into territories where I have low confidence in my architectural instincts though, so if anyone has built stuff like this, please contribute RFCs etc. Do we need a BLIP format? Blygger Improvements Proposal, like BIP/EIP/PIP?

Closing philosophy thought. I wrote a later post called [GUTS: The Grad Unified Theory of Striving and Slacking](https://ribbonfarm.com/2016/07/28/fat-thinking-and-economies-of-variety/) building on the fat thinking post. It had this 2x2 in it. I think by my analysis here, going by the near-biological level of client diversity we have right now (7 clients for 11 nodes last I checked), we’re firmly in the upper right Fat+Divergent “play” quadrant, and we should stay there. At least for a while.

See also:

>Any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from play (Seb Paquet)
